target_customer: Groups, event organizers, communities and nonprofits collecting money together; later developers via a group payments API
problem: Groups had no simple, secure way to pool money for trips, tailgates, gifts or causes without one person fronting the cash.
business_model: Transaction fee on money collected through campaigns, plus a developer API for group payments

founders.name: James Beshara
previous_startups: Dvelo (rebranded as Crowdtilt, per Wikipedia coverage)

founders.name: Khaled Hussein
founders.background_notes: YC page says he started young in Egypt, moved to the US, was named to a Time 30 under 30 list, and later founded RedDoor and Stipple.

exit.reason: Acqui-hire after the company ran low on capital; platform retired June 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Money movement, escrow-style collection and payment processor integration (Stripe, Balanced, Braintree) plus compliance for nonprofit fundraising are standard but fiddly for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Features were copyable and group payments could be added by payment apps; the API and compliance work added some friction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent shut it down, but the business was never profitable and Airbnb bought the team in 2017 and retired the product in June 2017.

market_need_then: Early coverage framed it as a Kickstarter for any group. Users raised about $1 million in the first three months after the February 2012 launch.

branding.name_origin: A tilt is described by the company as the moment a group reaches critical mass and unlocks something together; Crowdtilt was shortened to Tilt in July 2014.
branding.domain_note: tilt.com was used after the July 2014 rename; no source explains how it was acquired.

identity.logo: New name and logo introduced with the 2014 rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: Community framing, people coming together to create the world around them

rebrands.why: Part of a broader vision to be a general platform for funding all kinds of projects, per TechCrunch

branding.community_and_virality: Press covered the rename; Crowdfund Insider speculated about the cost of the domain. No merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Wide tech press coverage and a clean one-word name after the rebrand, but no source shows brand-driven growth.

pivots.to: Tilt as a broader social payments platform
pivots.why: Looked beyond the crowdfunding niche, per TechCrunch

outcome_analysis: Tilt raised large venture rounds (Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz in April 2013 and a reported Series B in December 2013) on fast early group-payment volume, but sources say it was never profitable and ran out of capital. Airbnb acquired the team in early 2017 as an acqui-hire and the platform was retired in June 2017, well below investor hopes given reports of over $60 million raised.
notes: No company website listed (YC page has none). Series A amount and the Series B amount and date come from Wikipedia summaries via search; the a16z post is cited for the Series A, and Series B investors were not found. The Wikipedia summary states a $12M price for the Airbnb deal, but I did not open a primary source, so it is not recorded. CB Insights style figures of $62.1M raised and a $400M valuation are single-aggregator and unverified. The stage of the seed is as stated by TechCrunch. An unrelated fintech named Tilt appears in searches; ignored.
